commitResults.messageTitle: Set up LittleDaisy with a greeting and a farewell
commitResults.messageBody: Rename Duke.java to LittleDaisy.java so the bot has its own identity, and print a figlet banner, a welcome line and a sign-off. say() takes varargs so replies of any length share the same divider styling.

Add a chat() loop between the greeting and the sign-off: read one trimmed line at a time and repeat it back, stopping on 'bye'. Guard the loop with hasNextLine() so input that ends without 'bye' exits cleanly instead of throwing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store user input as tasks and list them
commitResults.messageBody: Level-1 only echoed each line back. Keep the lines instead, in a fixed-size array of 100 as the increment allows, so that a list command can show them as a numbered list.

Introduce a Task class so a task carries its own done flag and knows how to render itself, instead of the chatbot holding bare strings. This keeps the display format next to the data, which the task subclasses in the next increment can then override.

Give each kind of task its own subclass of Task, so that the type icon and any extra times are rendered by the task itself. The list, mark and unmark code stays as it was, since it only ever asks a Task for its string form.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject bad input with friendly error messages
commitResults.messageBody: Introduce LittleDaisyException, thrown wherever input cannot be acted on: an unknown command, an empty description, a missing /by, /from or /to, or a task number that is absent, non-numeric or out of range. A single catch in the command loop prints the message, so the conversation survives every mistake instead of crashing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command, store tasks in an ArrayList
commitResults.messageBody: Removing from the middle of a plain array would mean shifting every later element by hand, so swap the array and its separate count for an ArrayList, which tracks its own size and closes the gap on remove. The delete command reuses parseTaskNumber, so bad task numbers are already handled.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace command-word strings with a Command enum
commitResults.messageBody: The eight command words were a closed set pretending to be free-form strings. An enum makes the set explicit, lets the dispatch become a switch the compiler can check for coverage, and folds unknown input into the same type via an UNKNOWN constant, so lookup never returns null.
